items.title: Finite-jet local operators and engineering dimension
items.design_state: Assigned item fully authored in Step 1; readiness is recorded separately.
items.statement: Use natural units $c=\hbar=1$ on four-dimensional Minkowski space $M=\mathbb R^{1,3}$ with coordinates $x^0=ct,x^1,x^2,x^3$ and metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$. Fix a complex affine algebraic group $G$ with no nontrivial closed normal unipotent subgroup, where unipotent means that every nonzero finite-dimensional rational module has a nonzero fixed vector; this is the reductive hypothesis. Fix a finite set $I$ of field species. For each $i\in I$, fix a finite-dimensional complex $\mathbb Z/2$-graded vector space $\Phi_i=\Phi_i^{\bar 0}\oplus\Phi_i^{\bar 1}$, a field parity, and an algebraic representation $\rho_i:G\to\operatorname{GL}(\Phi_i)$. Include the declared spacetime-index action in $G$ or in its specified finite-dimensional representation data. A field configuration assigns smooth component functions on $M$ to the even generators and formal odd Grassmann generators with smooth coefficient functions to the odd generators.

references.title: C. P. Burgess, Introduction to Effective Field Theory
Matthias Neubert, Effective Field Theory and Heavy Quark Physics (2004 TASI Lectures)

items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. items.title: Finite dimensionality of fixed-order local operator spaces
items.design_state: Locally added A-page prerequisite with a complete Step-1 argument; readiness is recorded separately.
items.statement: Let $J=J_{\bar 0}\oplus J_{\bar 1}$ be a finite-dimensional $\mathbb Z/2$-graded complex vector space with a finite homogeneous basis $z_1,\ldots,z_n$, each generator assigned a rational engineering weight. Form $P=\operatorname{Sym}(J_{\bar 0}^{*})\otimes\Lambda(J_{\bar 1}^{*})$. For finite $q\in\mathbb Z_{\geq0}$ and any $D\in\mathbb Q$, let $P_{q,D}$ be the span of supercommutative monomials of total generator degree at most $q$ and total engineering weight $D$. Then $P_{q,D}$ is finite-dimensional. If a group acts linearly on $J$ preserving parity and the weight grading, its invariant subspace $P_{q,D}^{G}$ is also finite-dimensional.

references.title: C. P. Burgess, Introduction to Effective Field Theory
Matthias Neubert, Effective Field Theory and Heavy Quark Physics (2004 TASI Lectures)

items.title: Finite-order invariant operator-basis quotient
items.design_state: Assigned item fully authored in Step 1; readiness is recorded separately.
items.statement: Fix a finite jet order $r$, maximum polynomial field degree $q$, engineering weight $D$, finite field-species list, coefficient field $\mathbb C$, and complex reductive affine algebraic group $G$ with the finite-dimensional rational action specified on the jet generators, including the declared spacetime-index symmetries. Let $W_D$ be the finite-dimensional space of all local polynomials of weight $D$ and degree at most $q$, before imposing $G$-invariance, and let $V_D=W_D^G$ be its invariant scalar subspace. An admitted raw relation space is a specified $G$-stable linear subspace $\widetilde R_D\leq W_D$, given by explicit linear identities among the chosen polynomials. Its invariant part is $R_D=\widetilde R_D\cap V_D$. Any action, boundary, or observable interpretation of the selected identities is extra mathematical data and must be stated with the result that verifies it.

items.title: Fixed-order integration-by-parts and leading-equation field-redefinition relations
items.design_state: Assigned item fully authored in Step 1; readiness is recorded separately.
items.statement: Assume full AC. Use four-dimensional natural units $c=\hbar=1$ and a finite jet-polynomial field model with its declared finite rational action of a complex reductive affine algebraic group $G$. Let $W_D$ be a finite raw local-polynomial space at fixed engineering weight $D$, derivative cutoff, and field-degree cutoff; let $V_D=W_D^G$. Let $\widetilde R_D$ be the $G$-stable linear span in $W_D$ of the declared polynomial identities, admitted total-divergence densities, and leading-equation densities $F^a\mathcal E_a^{(0)}$ defined below, with $R_D=\widetilde R_D\cap V_D$. The finite-order invariant operator quotient is $\mathcal Q_D=V_D/R_D$.

items.title: A dimension-six scalar operator reduced by integration by parts and the leading equation
items.design_state: Assigned item fully authored in Step 1; readiness is recorded separately.
items.statement: Let $M=\mathbb R^{1,3}$ have metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ and use natural units $c=\hbar=1$. Let $\phi:M\to\mathbb R$ be a smooth compactly supported real scalar field of engineering dimension one. Let $m\geq0$ and $\Lambda>0$ have mass dimension one, let $g,C\in\mathbb R$ be dimensionless, and let $\epsilon$ be a dimensionless formal parameter with $\epsilon^2=0$. For dimension bookkeeping, adjoin a central formal scalar $M_s$ of engineering weight one and specialize $M_s=m$ only after forming homogeneous expressions. Let $\widehat W_6$ be the finite complex vector space of polynomials of weight six in $M_s$ and the scalar field jets, with derivative cutoff two and field-degree cutoff six; take the symmetry group to be trivial. For compactly supported densities define $\mathcal I[f]=\int_M f\,d^4x$ and impose $\mathcal I(\partial_\mu J^\mu)=0$ for every compactly supported current.
